title: ai relay tells the orchestrator to record each step with relay-run
lead: `slicer ai relay` tells the orchestrator to call `relay-run begin` when a relay starts, `relay-run step` as each role and subagent starts and finishes, and `relay-run end` at the close, so the board has data without extra prompting.
findings_note: owner request, session 2026-10-14: monitor slice relays from the TUI
boundary: **Not in this slice:** the agents repo playbook (`multi-agent-workflows/playbooks/slice-relay.md`), which is outside this repository; the owner updates it separately.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: The ledger is only as good as the orchestrator's recording. `relay_text` (`src/slicer/ai.py:248`) is the relay contract the orchestrator reads, so the recording steps belong there, next to the role order in `RELAY_ORDER` (line 196).

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `src/slicer/ai.py`: `RELAY_ORDER` (line 196) gains the three recording steps with exact commands; the generic text (no project) includes them too.
- `docs/commands.md` (`ai relay` row), `CHANGELOG.md`.
- `tests/test_ai.py`.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
- `test_RelayText_NamesRelayRunBeginStepEnd`, in the project and generic variants
- `test_RelayText_RelayRunCommands_PassUnknownFlagCheck`: each backticked `slicer relay-run` command passes `check`'s unknown-flag scan.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Write the tests and watch them go red.
2. Add the text.
3. Update the docs and CHANGELOG.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: - The affected tests, then the full suite. `slicer check` passes.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: Worktree `.worktrees/s284`, branch `feature/s284-ai-relay-records`. Commit only on the branch.
